clue.text: Abandon hope of the French match

parts.note: French for 'of the' before a plural noun
to match things is to pair them

explanation.surface: Someone gives up all hope of winning a match against the French.
explanation.definitionFit: To despair is a verb meaning to lose or give up all hope.

clue.text: Obliterate retrograde N-word

indicators.note: retrograde means moving backwards, so the following word is read from its end

parts.note: taken letter by letter as written, without the hyphen

explanation.surface: A call to wipe out a backward-looking racist slur.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphenated term looks like a reference to a slur, but it is simply the letters N, W, O, R, D to be turned round into DROWN.
explanation.definitionFit: To drown something, such as a sound, is to swamp or blot it out completely.

clue.text: Arranges fixed time with the French

parts.note: something set is fixed
T is the standard abbreviation for time
French for 'the' with a plural noun

explanation.surface: Someone sets up a fixed appointment with French contacts.
explanation.definitionFit: To settle matters is to put them in order or resolve them, which is to arrange them.

clue.text: Content to draw a youth out

indicators.note: the content of something is what sits inside it, so the answer is held within the following words

parts.note: runs across the three words, from the end of the first into the start of the last

explanation.surface: Someone is happy to coax a young person out of their shell.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is out, not at home, is away; the two adverbs are synonyms of absence.

clue.text: Communists secretly plot to support unrest here arranged with two Democrats

indicators.note: in a down entry, what supports something sits beneath it, so this piece comes last
things arranged are put into a new order, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
D is the abbreviation for Democrat, twice
a plot of garden is a flower bed

explanation.surface: A Cold War scare: communists are covertly stirring up unrest here with the help of Democrats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reds under the bed' is the Cold War catchphrase for the fear of communists hidden everywhere in society.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom pictures communist agents lurking unseen, as if hiding beneath one's bed, so it means communists working covertly.

clue.text: Strong action I took over a lie

indicators.note: to take over is to step into another's place, so one letter displaces another

parts.note: F is forte, the musical direction for loud or strong
taken as written
taken as written; it replaces the A
taken as written; this letter is the one displaced

explanation.surface: Someone confesses that a lie led them to take drastic steps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I took over a' reads as a confession; it means the letter I takes the place of the letter A in the preceding word.
explanation.definitionFit: Fiction is something invented and untrue, so a made-up story or falsehood counts as a lie.

clue.text: Suddenly leave the control and hit the roof

definitions.meaning: first meaning, read literally: to fly off a handle you are holding
second meaning: to lose your temper all at once

explanation.surface: A driver lets go of the wheel and crashes into a ceiling.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half is a literal reading of the idiom, like an axe head flying off its handle; the second is its everyday sense.
explanation.definitionFit: To fly off the handle is an idiom for suddenly becoming furious, the same as hitting the roof.

clue.text: Scruples against knowledge based on experiments

parts.note: as in pros and cons
science is knowledge gained by experiment

explanation.surface: Someone has ethical objections to experiment-based research.
explanation.definitionFit: Scruples are moral qualms, and conscience is the inner moral sense that produces them.

clue.text: Entrance French artist at opening of show

parts.note: Jean-Auguste-Dominique Ingres, the 19th-century French painter

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter, so only that is kept

parts.note: the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A French painter makes an entrance at the start of an exhibition.
explanation.definitionFit: Ingress is a formal word for going in, or a way in, so it means an entrance.

clue.text: Turn on old volunteers with incomplete exam marks

indicators.note: to turn something round is to set it back to front

parts.note: taken as written, to be turned round

indicators.note: incomplete means missing a part, here its final letter

parts.note: the Territorial Army, the former name of Britain's volunteer reserve force
an exam is a test

explanation.surface: A grumble about old soldiers who scored poorly on an unfinished test.
explanation.walkthrough: TEST loses its last letter to give TES.
explanation.definitionFit: To notate is to write down in notation, so 'marks' as a verb, jotting something down, fits.

clue.text: Would try a change, apparently

indicators.note: making a change means the letters are altered into another order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written; the letter doubles as part of the signal

explanation.surface: It seems someone would like to try something different.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'a' does two jobs: it is a letter of the fodder and part of the phrase 'a change'.
explanation.definitionFit: Outwardly means judging by external appearance, which is what 'apparently' also conveys.

clue.text: Nearly left behind in the dark

parts.note: nigh is an old word for near or nearly

indicators.note: the part of a word behind the rest is its tail, so its final letter is taken

parts.note: the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: Someone was almost abandoned with no light to see by.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left behind' looks like one phrase meaning abandoned; here it says to take the end of 'left'.
explanation.definitionFit: Night is the period of darkness, and 'the dark' is a common phrase for nighttime.

clue.text: Industrial outskirts bordered by Tyneside river

indicators.note: something bordered is enclosed by an edge, so one piece sits inside another

parts.note: Tyneside is in the North East of England, abbreviated NE

indicators.note: the outskirts of a town are its edges, so only the outer letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: The factory fringes along the River Tyne, in north-east England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tyneside river' wants to be the Tyne; the river is the definition alone, and Tyneside, Newcastle's region, supplies the border.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nile is the great river of north-east Africa, flowing through Egypt.

clue.text: Fresh cuts in Fife are at the required level

indicators.note: something made fresh is produced anew, so these letters are given a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: New spending cuts in the Scottish county of Fife are judged adequate.
explanation.walkthrough: Fife is a county in eastern Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Sufficient means enough, adequate for the purpose, which is meeting the level needed.

clue.text: Criminal resents CIA's lack of co-operation

indicators.note: something criminal is crooked or wrong, so these letters are bent out of order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A crook resents the American spy agency's unhelpfulness.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after CIA is only the surface's possessive and gives no letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Resistance is opposition or refusal to comply, which is a failure to co-operate.

clue.text: Leading alpinist regularly sick at finish of climb

indicators.note: whatever is leading is at the front, so the first letter is wanted

parts.note: the first letter of the word

indicators.note: at regular intervals, so every other letter is taken

parts.note: the first and third letters
a finish is an end

explanation.surface: A mountaineer out in front feels ill at the top of the ascent.
explanation.definitionFit: To ascend is to go up, which is what climbing a slope or mountain does.

clue.text: Forces unopened locks

indicators.note: with no opening, the word loses its first letter

parts.note: stresses are physical forces acting on a body

explanation.surface: Someone forces locks that haven't been opened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Locks' looks like door locks; it means locks of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Tresses are long locks of a person's hair, so the two nouns are synonyms.

clue.text: Private note by princess reaches the Queen

indicators.note: one thing reaching another arrives next to it, so these pieces join up end to end

parts.note: sol (or soh) is the fifth note of the sol-fa scale
Di, short for Diana, Princess of Wales
ER, Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: A confidential letter from a princess arrives for the Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Private' reads as confidential; it is the army's lowest rank.
explanation.definitionFit: A private is a soldier of the lowest rank, so the noun names a type of soldier.

clue.text: Teaches in groups

definitions.meaning: first meaning: trains or educates, as a verb
second meaning: shoals of fish or whales, as a noun

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a description of group teaching; the two halves are separate senses of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: To school is to train someone, and schools are also large groups of fish swimming together.

clue.text: Top story's on earls regularly becoming prime ministers?

parts.note: the lead is a newspaper's main story

indicators.note: at regular intervals, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: the first, third and fifth letters

explanation.surface: A front-page story about aristocrats who rise to run the country.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that prime ministers are just one example of leaders.
explanation.definitionFit: Prime ministers head their governments and parties, so they are an example of leaders.

clue.text: Copy key shortly before breakout

indicators.note: said shortly, the word appears in its common short form, as printed on a keyboard
placed before means the piece just named comes first

parts.note: the Esc key on a computer keyboard
to ape is to imitate

explanation.surface: Duplicating a key is the first step of a prison break.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue names the copy first but 'before' puts the key in front.
explanation.definitionFit: A breakout is a getaway from prison, which is an escape.

clue.text: Starts to plague international body over the German spoils

indicators.note: in a down entry, what lies over another piece is written above it
the plural 'starts' asks for more than one opening letter, so the first two are kept

parts.note: the first two letters of the word
the United Nations
German for 'the' (masculine)

explanation.surface: A global organisation is beset by German problems over war booty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starts' is plural, so two opening letters are taken rather than one.
explanation.definitionFit: Plunder is goods taken by force, the spoils of war or theft.

clue.text: Directly competing to make for the top

parts.note: to head for a place is to make for it
taken as written
the head of a table or page is its top

explanation.surface: Rivals race one another to reach the summit.
explanation.definitionFit: A head-to-head contest is one where two rivals face each other in direct competition.

clue.text: Start showing doubt held by magistrate

indicators.note: something held by another is gripped inside it

parts.note: a Justice of the Peace, a lay magistrate in Britain
um is a sound of hesitation or doubt

explanation.surface: A judge begins to look uncertain.
explanation.definitionFit: To start is to jump, as when someone flinches from fright or surprise.

clue.text: Marginally inconvenienced after power faded away

indicators.note: coming after means the piece named first is placed second
keeping just the margins means the middle of the word is dropped

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for power in physics
taken as written; only its two letters at each edge stay

explanation.surface: Someone was slightly put out when the electricity failed.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking the two letters at each margin of INCONVENIENCED gives IN and ED.
explanation.definitionFit: To pine is to waste away through grief or longing, so pined means faded away.

clue.text: Sympathetic relative takes on daughter

indicators.note: to take something on is to add it to yourself, so the next piece is attached

parts.note: kin are one's relations
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A caring family member takes in a daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: A kind person is considerate and caring, which is what sympathetic means.

clue.text: Canoe could be Indian, possibly

indicators.note: what a word could be is another form it might take, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A canoe might be of Native American design.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Indian' pairs with canoe to suggest a Native American craft; it is the Indian Ocean, and 'possibly' marks an example.
explanation.definitionFit: The Indian is one of the world's oceans, so it is an example of the answer.

clue.text: Unable to stand being ordered to accept European doctor

indicators.note: to accept something is to take it in, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: bidden is the past participle of bid, to command
E is the abbreviation for European
Dr is the abbreviation for doctor

explanation.surface: Someone too weak to stand up is told to see a European doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: A bedridden person is confined to bed by illness or weakness and so cannot get up on their feet.

clue.text: American writer died after second stay

indicators.note: coming after means the pieces just named follow the next one

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second
US for American
a pen is a writing instrument
D is the abbreviation for died

explanation.surface: A US author passed away a moment later.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stay' sounds like remaining; here it is the legal sense, as in a stay of execution.
explanation.definitionFit: To stay a process is to halt or defer it, which is to suspend it.

clue.text: Stop welcoming horribly rude bore

indicators.note: to welcome someone is to take them in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to stop is to end

indicators.note: something done horribly is messed up, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A plea to stop admitting a terribly rude bore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bore' looks like a tedious person; it is the past tense of bear.
explanation.definitionFit: Bore, the past tense of bear, means put up with or suffered, just as endured does.
